# What Is Retrieval-Augmented Generation?

## Definition and Origins

Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a framework for AI that integrates large language models (LLMs) with external knowledge retrieval. The approach originated from a 2020 academic paper by Lewis et al., which proposed RAG as "a new framework for AI that seeks to integrate additional knowledge, such as organizational data, and generate results that can be linked to that knowledge." A key benefit of this design is that it "allows users to access information from within an organization and reduces the risk of hallucinations."

## From Research Concept to Commercial Technology

What began as an academic technique has evolved into a significant commercial technology stack. According to a MarketsandMarkets report published in October 2025, the RAG market was valued at USD 1.94 billion in 2025 and is projected to grow to USD 9.86 billion by 2030, reflecting a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 38.4%. This rapid growth reflects rising enterprise adoption of RAG-based systems.

Major technology companies—including Microsoft, AWS, Google, Anthropic, and Cohere—are actively building RAG infrastructure, indicating that RAG has become a core strategic focus for leading AI vendors rather than a niche research method.

## Practical Applications

One of the leading real-world applications of RAG is enterprise chatbots. A 2025 industry analysis highlights how RAG-powered chatbots deliver accurate, contextual responses by accessing real-time product documentation, FAQ databases, and support ticket histories. This allows businesses to ground customer-facing AI systems in current, verifiable information sources.

## Formalizing Evaluation

As RAG adoption has grown, so has the effort to rigorously evaluate these systems. The TREC 2025 RAG Track—the second edition of this benchmarking effort—continues to advance research on systems that integrate retrieval and generation to address complex, real-world information needs. Building on the inaugural 2024 track, the 2025 edition introduces more complex, multi-sentence query challenges, reflecting the maturation of RAG evaluation as a formal research discipline.

## Summary

Retrieval-augmented generation combines the generative capabilities of LLMs with external knowledge retrieval, enabling systems to link outputs to verifiable data sources and reduce the risk of hallucinations. Since its introduction in 2020, RAG has grown from an academic proposal into a rapidly expanding commercial market, adopted by major AI companies and increasingly benchmarked through formal evaluation efforts like TREC.
